title: How to Vet a Content Subscription Service
excerpt: A practical checklist for evaluating content subscription services, covering ownership, quality control, cadence, interlinking, and the contract terms that trip up business owners.
metaDescription: Learn what to look for in a content subscription service, from ownership terms to quality checks, so you pick a plan that actually builds organic visibility.

title: How B2B Software Content Should Map to Use Cases
excerpt: Most B2B software content is organized around features or generic topics. Organizing it around use cases attracts buyers who already match your product and shortens the qualification conversation.
metaDescription: A practical guide to content marketing for B2B software companies built around use cases, so you attract buyers who match your product and skip the tire-kickers.

title: Why Publishing Cadence Beats One Perfect Article
excerpt: A single excellent article rarely moves a business. A steady cadence of solid articles builds coverage, internal links, and topical depth that compounds. Here's the mechanics and a worked example.
metaDescription: Publishing cadence beats individual article quality over time because search visibility compounds. Here's how steady output builds coverage that one great post can't

title: B2B Software Content That Survives a Long Sales Cycle
excerpt: Most B2B software content targets people ready to buy today. That's a fraction of the market. Here's how to build content that works across a multi-month evaluation.
metaDescription: B2B software content marketing that matches a 3-9 month sales cycle. Map content to problem-aware, solution-aware, and vendor-comparison stages to close more deals.

title: Structuring B2B Software Content for the Buying Committee
excerpt: Most B2B software content targets one reader and ignores the four to seven people who actually approve the purchase. Here is how to map your content to the whole buying committee.
metaDescription: A practical guide to content marketing for B2B software companies: map content to the buying committee and buyer stages so more deals close faster.
